A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QUIDS research. Their full text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison despite substantial rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Q2ID experiments, component ablations, human and LLM evaluations, and attention-based case analysis in Section 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds o3 comparisons, parameter sensitivity experiments and a failure case.

M1.justification: The dual encoder, contrastive decoder, relevant-minus-irrelevant hidden-state combination, IDNA procedure and training losses remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 restates v1's negative-augmentation steps; renaming Dual Space Modeling to DualSM does not introduce a component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Q2ID coverage: TREC Dynamic Domain and Robust collections plus English SemEval community question answering. The new sensitivity experiments and Doha case remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds OpenAI o3 in zero-shot and two-shot settings to Table 1. The existing CtrsGen, T5/BART, LLaMa3.1 and QFS comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The reported human panel increases from three to five PhD students, retaining 50 samples and the four 1–5 criteria. New loss-weight and IDNA-threshold sweeps introduce controlled settings. The main data split, training budget, default parameters and stated automatic metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, intent-type breakdowns and Freon-12 case, v3 adds IDNA-threshold sensitivity (Figure 6b), loss-weight sensitivity (Appendix B.2/Table 5), and a Doha failure case (Appendix E/Figure 7). These substantially expand evidence about parameter dependence and contextual filtering failures.

E5.justification: v1 reports five experimental runs; v3 explicitly identifies five random seeds in Table 1, clarifying their basis without establishing an increased run count. Paired t-tests and the 20-sample GPT-4o scoring procedure are retained; confidence intervals are not added.

E6.justification: v3 adds o3 results, including ROUGE-1 of 34.91 versus QUIDS-BART's unchanged 34.47, plus sensitivity and failure findings. Human ratings and correlations change with the enlarged panel; human inclusion now favors exploratory over informational queries. Figure 6a also displays roughly half v1's input-length scores without explaining the scaling. Existing Table 1 rows and Table 2 values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The task formulation and mathematical content of Equations 1–10 are retained. v3's Equation 11 merely numbers the LLM scoring formula already given in v1 Section 4.4. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly frames outputs as post-retrieval proxies for system-inferred intent, excluding mechanistic explanations of the ranker and emphasizing exploratory search. The method contributions remain, while the introduction strengthens the performance claim to significant superiority in human evaluation.

C2.justification: v3 adds explicit training-efficiency and dataset-coverage limitations, connects the Doha failure to commonsense or domain-knowledge requirements, and interprets parameter sensitivity and o3's verbose outputs. Existing interpretations of intent-type differences and document length are largely retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds a QUIDS code-availability link and documents configurations supporting loss-weight selection. Most training, decoding and baseline implementation details are relocated into Appendix B rather than changed.

R1.justification: v3 substantially refocuses research positioning on post-retrieval feedback versus retrieval optimization and content summarization. Appendix A/Table 6 adds a structured comparison with query understanding, QFS and pseudo-relevance feedback. Query2doc, ConvGQR and other query-expansion references are added while much of the earlier classification and retrieval survey is pruned.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method explanations are extensively rewritten. Experimental analyses are regrouped, settings and interpretations move into descriptive Appendices A–F, and repeated evaluation prompts become a shared template with metric-specific sections. The title and terminology also change.

P2.justification: Typography and figure/table placement change throughout. Rating plots become wide panels with 1–5 axes instead of 1–3; new sensitivity, task-comparison and failure displays are added, and the correlation table gains averages. However, v3's case-study captions reverse the with/without-irrelevant-document labels relative to the panels.

improvement.justification: The added o3 comparison, parameter checks, failure analysis and code disclosure make QUIDS easier to scrutinize. Clearer post-retrieval framing and explicit limitations also improve the paper. These gains are tempered by unexplained input-length score changes, reversed case-study captions and inconsistent statements about o3's ROUGE performance.
